statement: A snail is at 12 on a number line. It crawls along the line to 5. How many steps does it crawl, if each step goes from one number to the next?

choices.misconception: I counted only the numbers in between, leaving out both 12 and 5.
I counted the numbers from 12 down to 5, both ends included, instead of the steps between them.
I gave the number where the snail started.
I added 12 and 5 instead of finding the distance between them.

hints: Count the jumps, not the numbers.
The distance between two numbers on a number line is the number of steps between them. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one, or count the jumps one at a time.
Jump from 12 to 11, 11 to 10, and so on until you reach 5. Count each jump once.

solutions.reliable: The steps go 12 to 11, 11 to 10, 10 to 9, 9 to 8, 8 to 7, 7 to 6 and 6 to 5. That is 7 steps, the same as $12 - 5 = 7$. The idea to keep: the distance on a number line counts the jumps, so the starting number is not counted.

whyOnTest: Distance on a number line is a difference, and counting the marks instead of the jumps gives one too many.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
